audit.whatIsWrong: The stage sides contradict the data and the packet flagged it: Aatrox wins only 47.92% over 4,524 games, yet the chart hands Aatrox 5 of 7 stages.
audit.why: The lane genuinely does favour Aatrox pre-armour, but the losing overall win rate means the two losing stages are much heavier than the chart implies. The prose, not the counts, is where that has to land.
audit.corrected: Left the entry counts alone (not writable without breaking the mirror) and made the early prose conditional on breaking Granite Shield, which is what actually decides whether the "winning" stages materialise. Flagged for the user in questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike said "his R Unstoppable Force" with no cooldown.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s. At 130s a spent ult is a two-minute free window — that is the concrete reason the 3-6 stages are yours, and it deserves the number.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1] now carry the 130s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield was described only as "a free shield" with no size and no recharge rule.
audit.why: Riot's text: it absorbs damage up to 10% of his maximum health and "if Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds, this effect recharges". That makes chip damage before a commit mechanically correct rather than optional, and it is the single most useful thing to know in this lane.
audit.corrected: early and mid now state the 10% max-health size and the out-of-combat recharge, and tie a chip auto to keeping it down.

edits.before: You hold the edge at levels 1-2 before Malphite has armor items. His passive gives him a free shield to absorb some poke and his Q slow lets him chip you while backing off, but he can't fight you and your base brawl beats his. Don't waste E aggressively; you'll need it later to escape his R. Trade for even-or-better CS, chip his shield down, and press your dominance while his defenses are still thin.
edits.after: You hold the edge at levels 1-2 before Malphite has armour items. Granite Shield gives him a free shield worth 10% of his max health and Seismic Shard (Q) steals your Move Speed while he backs off, but he can't fight you and your base brawl beats his. Don't waste E aggressively; you need it to escape his R. Trade for even-or-better CS, break the shield before you commit, and press while his defences are thin.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 6 all favor you and this is your kill window: before Malphite has meaningful armor items, land your Q3 sweetspot knockup into E and drain him hard in every trade he steps into. Even at 6 your pre-armor combo out-damages him — just respect that his R Unstoppable Force is a point-and-click engage that can negate the combo and hand his jungler a free kill, so save E to dash out of the R rather than to chase. The lane only flips once his first armor item comes online, so cash your lead before then.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 6 all favour you and this is your kill window: before Malphite has meaningful armour items, land your Q3 sweetspot knockup into E and drain him hard in every trade he steps into. Break Granite Shield first — it only recharges after a few seconds without being hit, so a chip auto keeps it down. Even at 6 your pre-armour combo out-damages him; just respect that Unstoppable Force (R) is a 130s point-and-click engage that hands his jungler a kill, so save E to dash out of it, not to chase. Cash your lead before his first armour item.

edits.before: Use passive shield to eat your poke for free
edits.after: Recharge Granite Shield to eat your poke free

edits.before: You still out-brawl him at 6 before his armor lands, but his R Unstoppable Force is a point-and-click knockup that sets up ganks — respect it, don't shove blind, and save E to dash away from the engage.
edits.after: You still out-brawl him at 6 before his armour lands, but Unstoppable Force is a 130s point-and-click knockup that sets up ganks — respect it, don't shove blind, and save E to dash away from the engage.

edits.before: Bait or dodge R Unstoppable Force with your E dash
edits.after: Bait or dodge the 130s Unstoppable Force with your E

notes: Packet defect "level chart contradicts data" is real and unresolved — the chart gives Aatrox 5/7 stages at a 47.92% win rate. Stage sides/counts were not changed here because they are mirrored. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag that Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only), so no grounding claim was made in this slice.
